messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Warning: Size bias adjustment has increased expected cluster size.
parts:
Iakha

Distance has provided you with a warning, suggesting that something unexpected occurred when analysing your data.  I suggest you look at section 3.5 of Buckland et al. (2001) that discusses analysis of data for animals that occur in clusters.

An important element of analysing such data is the estimation of average cluster size.  This is made difficult because large clusters are more likely to be seen at large distances than small clusters; hence the average of detected clusters is likely larger than the average size of clusters in the population.  This is termed the "size bias" problem.  By default, Distance performs a regression in an attempt to remove this size bias, and produce an adjusted estimate of "expected cluster size". 

The expectation is that this adjusted estimate will be smaller that the observed average cluster size.  The warning message in your case states this is not the case, an instead the adjusted estimate is larger that the observed average cluster size.  There are several reasons that may cause this.  Often, this arises because of small numbers of clusters either in the study or in strata within the study area.  I suggest you examine the number of observations in your data and the observed cluster sizes.  It may be the case there is no size bias in your data and you were able to see clusters of all sizes equally well at all distances.  If you believe this to be the case, you can select the option in Distance on the Cluster Size tab of the Model Definition Properties to "Use mean of observed clusters"  (see below)
